paper_title: Acquiescence Is Not Personality: Why Human Psychometric Instruments Fail on Large Language Models

citation_statistics.comparison_to_baseline: ≈110% of the ACL/EMNLP baseline of ~52 citations per paper; the intro+RW alone cite 57 unique works.
citation_statistics.notes: Citations span 1936 (Mahalanobis) through 2026, integrate four distinct literatures (LLM personality profiling, silicon samples, response-style/acquiescence theory, RLHF/sycophancy/refusal), and provide explicit foundational anchors (Cronbach 1951; Couch & Keniston 1960; Crowne & Marlowe 1960; Kaiser 1958, 1960; Horn 1965; Tucker 1951; Meredith 1993; Vandenberg & Lance 2000) alongside recent 2024–2026 work (Suhr et al. 2025; Pelet et al. 2025; Han et al. 2025; Acerbi et al. 2024; Salecha et al. 2024).

coverage_and_completeness.justification: 57 unique citations in the literature-review portion sit at roughly 110% of the assumed ACL/EMNLP baseline. The review covers four relevant subareas with foundational and recent work in each; obvious omissions are minimal. Citation Coverage anchor: count is 80%–120% of Reference → 'Solid breadth if well integrated', which the structured 3-subsection organisation supports.

relevance_and_focus.justification: Citations align tightly with the central thesis (psychometric validity audit driven by alignment-induced acquiescence). The few statistical-methods anchors (Mahalanobis, Efron bootstrap) are scoped to the persona stress test and not citation padding. Some citations to broad survey methodology cluster around the response-style subsection, which is appropriate given the paper's framing of acquiescence as a survey-methodology import.

critical_analysis_and_synthesis.justification: Each Related Work subsection ends with an explicit limitation hypothesis and 'bridge to our method' synthesis rather than paper-by-paper summaries. The directional-asymmetry framing unifies sycophancy (Perez 2023; Sharma 2024) with safety-driven rejection (Bai 2022) as a single mechanism. Section 2.2 explicitly imports and contextualises the human-subject response-style toolkit. Falls short of 'exceptional' because the synthesis is concentrated rather than woven through each cluster.

positioning_and_novelty.justification: The positioning is unambiguous: 'to our knowledge, not previously documented in a single audit' explicitly differentiates the work from the single-instrument, single-check pattern in prior LLM-personality studies. The gap statement is literature-grounded with specific named limitations (single-instrument designs, response-style toolkit not imported, no item-level directional decomposition). The bridge to method is concrete (six-check battery + persona stress test + 4-instrument design).

organization_and_writing.justification: Logical flow from hook (Big Five LLM scoring + silicon samples) → measurement-question gap → causal-chain preview → contributions. Three Related-Work subsections are well-named and parallel-structured (overview → recent work → limitation → our bridge). Writing is clean academic prose with limited verbosity; figure references to causal_chain_overview and validation_battery_schema are well-placed.

citation_practices_and_rigor.justification: Every substantive claim is cited; the foundational/recent balance is appropriate (Cronbach 1951 through 2026). All cited works appear in refs.bib (verified by orphan-cite gate: 0 missing). Density is appropriate to section length. The Sociability sign-reversal claim in §4.6 is cited but cited only via the convergent-validity number rather than a methodological source, a minor weakness.

penalties.reason: Slight repetition of the directional-asymmetry framing across both Introduction and Related Work §2.2 (the same Δ=+0.29/Δ=-0.33 pair appears in both, with similar prose).

strengths: Explicit literature-grounded gap statement: 'to our knowledge, not previously documented in a single audit'.
Clean parallel structure across the three Related-Work subsections (overview → SOTA → limitation → bridge).
Foundational-to-recent citation balance with verified BibTeX coverage.
Directional-asymmetry framing unifies sycophancy and safety-driven refusal as a single mechanism, a non-trivial synthesis.
Citation count at ≈110% of the assumed venue baseline.
weaknesses: Some redundancy between the Introduction's mechanism preview and Related Work §2.2's discussion of acquiescence.
Critical-analysis synthesis is strongest in the 'bridge' sentences and weaker in the body of each subsection.
Forced-choice / ipsative alternatives (Brown & Maydeu-Olivares 2011) are flagged but not engaged in depth.
Silicon-sample programme is referenced as the downstream stakeholder but not connected to specific empirical claims about how validity failure would propagate.
top_improvements: Tighten or merge the directional-asymmetry mention so it appears in either the Intro or §2.2 but not both.
Add 1–2 sentences in §2.1 that explicitly link the silicon-sample failure mode to one or two concrete simulation tasks (e.g., opinion polling, economic experiments).

Strengthen §2.2 by explaining why forced-choice / IRT-fitted alternatives might or might not survive the LLM regime — this is currently flagged as future work rather than integrated into the gap statement.
